messages:
alex: Heads-up — ran into multiple customers confused by the Quickstart JS examples. The Node example uses `require('@redwood/inference')` and the ESM example uses `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'`, but our published package currently exports only named bindings (e.g. `export const RedwoodClient`).

morgan: Ugh, we've seen this in support tickets. Common error is `TypeError: Redwood is not a constructor` or `Cannot use import statement outside a module` depending on runtime. :facepalm:

jamie: Specific runtimes affected? Node CJS vs ESM, or also edge (Cloudflare/Vercel Edge Runtime)?

alex: Both. In Node CJS people do `const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')` expecting default export and then call `new Redwood()` — fails. In ESM it's usually fine if using named import but our docs show default in some places. Edge runtimes add another wrinkle because some bundlers/tree-shakers change export shape.

morgan: Repro steps I have in a gist: `node -e "const R=require('@redwood/inference'); console.log(R)"` shows `{ RedwoodClient: [Function], ... }` — no `default`.

jamie: For TS users, typings currently declare `export declare class RedwoodClient {}` and `export default RedwoodClient` is missing. So `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` typechecks in some setups via `esModuleInterop` but breaks in pure ESM and edge.

alex: Short term: we should update docs to consistently show named imports (`import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` and `const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference')`). Also add note about `esModuleInterop` and edge bundlers.

morgan: Agreed. Long term we could publish both a named export and a `default` property on CommonJS build (`module.exports.default = module.exports.RedwoodClient`) so `require` + default works. Also add `export default RedwoodClient` for ESM build.

jamie: I'll draft a minimal PR for docs and a follow-up PR for the package build. Proposed doc snippet:

```
// ESM
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })

// CJS
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference')
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
```

alex: Perfect. Also add an "Edge runtime" note: "If using Vercel Edge / Cloudflare Workers, ensure your bundler preserves named exports or use the ESM build. Avoid relying on `esModuleInterop` in those environments."

morgan: I've started a docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/212 — it updates Quickstart and adds a troubleshooting FAQ. Can someone review? @jamie @alex

jamie: Reviewing now. Will also open a small publish/build PR to add `module.exports.default = exports.RedwoodClient` and `export default RedwoodClient` in the ESM output. That should cover the common patterns.

docs-bot: New docs PR created by morgan: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/212 (title: "clarify require vs import in Quickstart")

deploy-bot: docsite deploy queued for PR 212 — preview URL: https://deploy-preview-212.docs.redwood.dev :rocket:

alex: Thanks — let's aim to merge docs PR today and ship the package change in next patch release. I'll add a short blurb to the changelog and a note in the release notes about compatibility fixes. :shipit:
